Enough grounding in measurement concepts (calibration, inter-rater reliability, sampling, rubric design) to independently set up and own the quality of our evaluation loop yourself
Experience with running quantitative and qualitative data analyses, interpreting and running statistical tests on evaluation data (natively or with AI tool support), and communicating conclusions to various stakeholders
A record of scaling and streamlining evaluation quality processes under shipping pressure, with a bias toward documentation and reproducibility over one-off analysis
Ability to work deeply with domain experts (e.g., ALR / lawyers) and translate nuanced judgment into repeatable, documented standards
Strong cross-functional coordination across Product, Engineering, Research, ALR, and data providers/vendors
Clear communicator who can build credibility and trust with stakeholders
Bias to action and high ownership, from writing the guideline to auditing a vendor batch line by line

Experience owning quality across multiple markets, languages, or jurisdictions
Built calibration, inter-rater reliability, or capability-tracking systems for annotation or evaluation pipelines
Experience transitioning evaluation work in-house or otherwise improving evaluation ROI
Familiarity with LLM-as-judge / automated evaluation used alongside human eval

Job Description
As the Supply Planning & Optimisation Manager, you will play a critical role in ensuring Youfoodz consistently meets customer demand through highly accurate planning, scheduling, inventory management, and capacity modelling. This leadership position is central to our mission, bridging the gap between commercial demand and factory execution to ensure our fulfillment teams have exactly what they need to deliver on time, every time.
This role is based in Karawatha and reporting to the Chief Operating Officer.
You will…
Own the end-to-end demand planning and production scheduling process for all B2B and B2C channels, partnering closely with Retail Sales and B2C commercial teams.
Drive Delivered In Full (DIF) metrics, guaranteeing that Pick & Pack, Line Haul, and DCs receive the exact volumes required.
Optimise inventory holding levels for finished goods and WIP food while minimising waste and obsolescence.
Lead short, medium, and long-term capacity planning in collaboration with Manufacturing and Engineering teams.
Partner with Manufacturing Leads to drive Continuous Improvement (CI) and optimise Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).
Act as the primary Operations representative and SME for major retail customers, managing retailer shelf-life expectations and DIFOT.
Lead the transition from S&OP to a mature, data-driven IBP model, facilitating cross-functional alignment.
Lead, coach, and evolve a team of 4 direct reports, driving transformation through automation and analytical problem-solving.
You have…
5+ years of experience in demand planning, production scheduling, or S&OP/IBP roles within an FMCG/food manufacturing environment.
Tertiary qualification in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or Engineering; APICS certification is highly regarded.
Proficiency in planning systems and data/AI tools, with the ability to lead system development and automation.
Proven capacity planning experience including OEE, labour modelling, and production sequencing.
You are…
An analytical leader who proactively solves complex supply chain challenges.
A strategic thinker capable of driving operational transformation and S&OP/IBP maturity.
A collaborative partner who can bridge commercial demand and factory execution.
An advocate for continuous improvement and operational efficiency.
A skilled negotiator and SME capable of managing critical retail partner relationships.

You’ll join a collaborative, diverse team from world-class companies like Apple, Affirm, Unity, and Visa, backed by renowned VC's including Thrive, a16z, Griffin Gaming, Ribbit, and Renegade. If you want to build disruptive technology, challenge the status quo, and help game creators thrive on their own terms, read on.

Neon is a gaming-focused Merchant of Record platform serving game publishers globally. We process payments across 50+ markets through multiple PSPs simultaneously, operating as the seller of record across card networks, local wallets, A2A rails, and alternative payment methods.
This role owns the operational backbone of that system: dispute and chargeback management, fraud operations, compliance monitoring, payment performance tracking, and operational support for Customer Success.

As the senior operator across these functions, the Payment Operations Manager sets operational standards, defines targets, owns PSP and partner operational relationships, and is accountable for outcomes across payments, risk, fraud, and compliance.

The role partners with the Head of Payments and the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader as a peer across all four functions.
This is a senior individual-contributor role . The Manager title reflects the seniority and ownership scope of the role and function, not direct reports at this stage.

Dispute & Chargeback Operations
Own dispute intake, evidence compilation, and resolution across all active payment processors and markets.
Define and own resolution SLAs and win-rate targets; identify systemic patterns and drive fixes with product and risk leads.
Prioritize and drive the roadmap for internal dispute tooling as operational infrastructure matures.
Fraud Operations
Own fraud operations and oversee investigations and transaction reviews in partnership with the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader.
Set monitoring and escalation standards across screening and decisioning tools; maintain case integrity and decision quality.
Track fraud loss trends across markets and game titles; surface and act on emerging attack patterns before they scale.
Payment Performance Monitoring
Own tracking of authorization rates, payment success rates, decline codes, and fraud losses across processors and markets.
Own post-launch metric reviews for new payment methods against defined performance thresholds.
Define the operational dashboard and alerting standard; ensure anomalies are caught before they become publisher-impacting incidents.
Customer Success Support
Serve as the senior operational point of contact for payment-related requests escalated by Customer Success.
Lead deep dives into publisher payment performance, dispute trends, and fraud exposure, producing structured analysis CS can use directly in publisher conversations.
Own the operational response to payment incidents: root cause investigation, timeline reconstruction, and remediation communication.
PSP & Partner Management
Own day-to-day operational relationships with PSPs and payment partners, including performance reviews, escalations, and issue resolution.
Hold partners accountable to performance and SLA commitments; drive improvement where markets or methods underperform.
Process, Tooling & Standards
Set and maintain operational standards, runbooks, and process documentation that others follow.
Prioritize automation opportunities and partner with the Head of Payments, Risk & Compliance, and engineering to translate operational gaps into product and tooling improvements.
Act as the senior escalation point for payment operations.
Key Success Metrics
Dispute win rate and resolution turnaround, owned and improved per processor.
Fraud operations outcomes: fraud loss rate, false positive rate, detection rate, and escalation accuracy.
PSR performance against target across active payment methods and markets, with defined review triggers on all methods.
Incident response and resolution time for publisher-impacting payment issues.
Reporting accuracy, on-time delivery, and operational process maturity as the function scales.
Ideal Profile
6-8+ years in payments operations, fraud ops, or fintech risk, with a track record of owning a function or leading operational initiatives, ideally at a PSP, Merchant of Record, or digital goods company.
Has run these functions end to end, not just participated in them; comfortable operating across multiple payment processors simultaneously, with direct experience of global PSPs such as Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, or Razorpay.
Experience owning PSP or partner relationships and influencing product, engineering, and Customer Success without formal authority.
Deep understanding of dispute and chargeback mechanics at the card network level (Visa/Mastercard rules), not just tool navigation.
Strong analytical capability: works across dashboards and data tools, builds structured reports, and finds signals in noisy transaction data.
Detail-oriented and self-directing; operates with significant autonomy across a broad and growing operational surface.
Business-level English proficiency required, written and verbal.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Alongside our model releases, Anthropic ships a steady stream of launches across the rest of the portfolio — products like Claude, Claude Code, and the developer platform; solutions for enterprises and startups; and the safeguards work that keeps Claude safe and trustworthy. Each launch brings product, engineering, policy, legal, communications, sales, and every part of marketing together around a single moment.
You'll be the central organizer of the product launch process for the product marketing team. You'll build and run the operating system behind it: the launch calendar, the plan of record for every deliverable, the path materials take through review, and execution on launch day. You'll treat the launch process itself as a product and drive adoption through influence.
In a portfolio this broad, not everything can get the same attention, so you'll focus your time on the team's top priorities, putting the most energy behind the launches that matter most and keeping the rest running on the systems you've built.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role on a lean product marketing team. When launch volume peaks, you'll contribute directly as a product marketer across all products and surfaces. If you've run launches where many moving parts had to converge at the same time, and you'd rather design the system than run it by hand, we'd like to meet you.

Serve as one of the core organizers of the product launch process end to end: collaborating with peers across product, operations, and GTM
Own the product launch calendar and sequencing across a broad portfolio of releases — products, solutions, and programs — prioritizing your time against the team's top priorities and coordinating timing with partner teams across marketing, product, and communications
Own the plan of record for each launch, like deliverables, owners, dependencies, and deadlines, and surface risks early enough to act on them
Own the path launch materials take through review, partnering with legal, policy, product, and communications so reviews happen in the right sequence against dates people can plan to
Drive decisions and alignment across senior cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority
Own launch-day execution: sequencing, timing, access, and the operational readiness of everything that goes live together
Own the internal resources our field teams reach for first, along with the operational side of enablement, including scheduling, speakers, and materials logistics
Develop and improve launch processes, playbooks, and operational frameworks that scale beyond any one launch
Own launch retrospectives, recurring product communications, and — when volume requires it — launch materials themselves

Have built or substantially improved a launch or release process
Treat process as a product — you care whether people adopt what you build, and you measure it
Background in product marketing, product operations, technical program management, and launch production all fit
Work well when priorities and timelines shift, and can keep a complex plan coherent as details change
Are effective at driving decisions across senior stakeholders without direct authority
Have a technical background with the ability to understand and communicate complex AI concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
Write clearly, and can produce launch-ready material

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems.
This role will take on new, ambiguous, or underdeveloped operational risks and help mature them into scalable capabilities. We work across USRO and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Legal, Safety, Support, and external vendors or partnership stakeholders.

We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas.
You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process.

You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks.
The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring.

You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop.
Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.
Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.
In This Role, You Will
Take ownership of ambiguous, high-priority safety and risk problems: define the problem, gather the right evidence, choose a practical path, drive execution, and close the loop.
Analyze structured and unstructured data, both quantitative and qualitative. This may include user reports, case narratives, conversations, escalations, and operational metrics to identify patterns, risks, and the highest-leverage interventions.
Build and test lightweight workflows, tools, automations, and decision aids that improve speed, quality, and consistency, then iterate based on real-world use.
Turn one-off insights and manual work into scalable operating mechanisms without adding unnecessary process or complexity.
Lead sensitive investigations, incident response, or launch-readiness work, including safety workflows, human review, escalation paths, partner coordination, and operational monitoring for product launches or cloud deployments.
Work directly with cross-functional and external partners to clarify ownership, resolve operational gaps, and turn incomplete signals into clear recommendations and decisions.
Measure whether the work is improving outcomes—such as quality, speed, coverage, operator effort, or risk reduction—and adjust quickly when it is not.
Help junior operators build judgment and independence through coaching, calibration, and reusable tools.
You Might Thrive in This Role If You
Have 8+ years of experience in trust and safety operations, investigations, incident response, product operations, technical program management, or another high-judgment, data-heavy operational field.
Have a track record as a scrappy generalist who can enter an unfamiliar problem, learn quickly, and deliver with limited structure or support.
Are highly data savvy, including the ability to make sense of messy qualitative or unstructured information and combine it with quantitative evidence.
Are technically fluent and hands-on with AI tools, dashboards, and data tooling, and can build or prototype practical solutions without waiting for a dedicated technical team.
Operate independently, make clear tradeoffs, and maintain momentum as priorities and requirements change.
Think in systems: you look beyond the immediate task and build approaches that can be repeated, measured, and operated by others.
Exercise strong judgment in sensitive situations involving user impact, policy, legal risk, technical constraints, and business priorities.
Communicate clearly and directly, especially in writing, and can drive decisions across teams without formal authority.

Experience in trust and safety, fraud, product safety, integrity, or another adversarial or high-severity risk domain.
Experience moving a new or immature workflow from early investigation into stable, scaled operations.
Experience supporting cloud platforms or deployment partnerships, enterprise products, product launches, connected devices, or other technically complex programs. Direct cloud experience is a plus, not a requirement.
Familiarity with SQL, lightweight scripting, no-code tools, workflow automation, or AI-assisted development.
Experience with vendor operations, quality programs, calibrations, or distributed operational teams.

As we scale, we are looking for a Marketing Operations Manager to build and manage the infrastructure that connects our marketing activity with sales. This is a hands-on role focused on making HubSpot a powerful operating system for understanding contact engagement, identifying intent signals, delivering relevant nurture, and helping our sales team engage the right people at the right time.
This is not an inbound lead-generation or MQL-focused role. The objective is to understand how contacts are engaging with Tangible over time — what they are reading, which campaigns they respond to, what they do on our website, and other relevant signals — so that we can identify increasing levels of interest and act quickly.

HubSpot & Marketing Operations
Own and manage Tangible's HubSpot marketing operations architecture.
Build, maintain and optimise HubSpot workflows, properties, lists, segmentation, campaigns and automation.
Ensure HubSpot is correctly structured to capture and connect engagement data across marketing channels.
Develop robust processes for tracking contact engagement across email, website activity, content consumption, campaigns and other relevant touchpoints.
Maintain data quality, contact lifecycle processes and the overall integrity of the marketing database.
Identify opportunities to improve the way HubSpot supports Marketing and Sales as the business scales.
Ensure marketing activity is properly tracked and connected to the CRM so engagement can be understood at an individual contact level.
Engagement Scoring & Intent Signals
Build and continuously refine contact engagement scoring based on meaningful behavioural signals.

Combine signals such as content engagement, website activity, email interactions, campaign participation and other relevant behaviours.
Use scoring to help Sales identify who is becoming more engaged and who should be contacted sooner .
Continuously test and refine scoring logic based on what actually proves useful to Sales.
Clearly communicate engagement signals and changes in contact behaviour to the sales team.
Ensure scoring is used as a prioritisation and intelligence tool, rather than simply as an inbound lead/MQL qualification model.
Nurture & Marketing Automation
Design, build and manage nurture programmes in HubSpot.
Develop segmented nurture journeys based on audience, interests, engagement and stage of relationship.
Manage the messaging, sequencing and logic behind automated campaigns.

Monitor campaign performance and continuously optimise programmes based on engagement and commercial outcomes.

Develop and manage marketing messaging for nurture campaigns, email campaigns and other targeted communications.
Support Sales with relevant outreach messaging, follow-ups, campaign assets and other enablement materials.
Use engagement data and audience behaviour to inform messaging and help Sales personalise outreach.
Help Sales understand how to interpret and act on engagement signals coming from HubSpot.

Report on which content is generating meaningful engagement and signals of interest.

Provide leadership and Sales with actionable insight rather than vanity metrics.
Identify patterns in contact behaviour and engagement that can inform marketing and sales activity.
Measure the effectiveness of nurture programmes, scoring models and marketing campaigns.
Continuously improve the marketing operations infrastructure based on data, feedback and commercial outcomes.

Partner with Sales to ensure engagement signals are genuinely useful in day-to-day prospecting and relationship management.
Help establish the processes and infrastructure required as Tangible's marketing and sales activity scales.
Act as the internal owner and subject-matter expert for HubSpot marketing operations.

Category-defining tech. Career-defining work.
For more than a decade, Cockroach Labs has built database technology trusted to power some of the world's most mission-critical applications. Now, as AI transforms how software is created and operated, the infrastructure behind it has to keep pace. Cockroach Continuum is built to meet this moment, bringing individual databases together into one fleet designed for agentic applications, where AI agents help teams provision, scale, and optimize workloads at machine speed.
The customers you’ll work with are some of the most innovative businesses in the world, and the problems they’re trying to solve are real and urgent. You’ll bring a genuinely differentiated product to a market moving fast, at a company positioned to lead it. The people who thrive here are the ones who want to own that opportunity.

GTM Operations is a small, high-intensity team at the center of Cockroach Labs' revenue transformation. As a Strategy & Ops Manager on this team, you'll work at the intersection of data, AI, and GTM execution -- building the analytical frameworks, agentic workflows, and operational programs that reshape how we create pipeline, accelerate deals, forecast revenue, and expand customer relationships.
This role requires real technical fluency. You'll query databases, build financial models, design AI-powered workflows, and measure their impact, all in service of transforming how our revenue organization operates. If you thrive in ambiguity, move faster than the organization expects, and believe the best strategy is one that actually gets deployed, this role was built for you.
To be eligible for this role, you must be based in London and will be expected to go into our office on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays.

AI Workflow Design and Execution: Design, deploy, and iterate on agentic workflows across the revenue org -- account prioritization agents, outreach personalization, pipeline intelligence, customer health scoring. Measure real performance outcomes and use that data to improve.
GTM Analytics and Insights: Query databases, analyze go-to-market performance data, and surface insights that inform how leadership allocates resources, sets targets, and structures the revenue org. Translate complexity into clear, actionable recommendations.
Financial Modeling and Business Cases: Build the financial models that translate AI initiatives and GTM programs into measurable revenue impact including pipeline coverage, conversion rates, rep productivity, deal velocity. Make the numbers tell the story.
Territory and Capacity Planning: Own analyses that support territory design, capacity planning, and coverage model decisions using data-driven frameworks. Help ensure the sales org is structured to hit its targets.
Cross-Functional Program Execution: Drive programs end-to-end by diagnosing operational bottlenecks, designing solutions, coordinating across stakeholders, and making sure adoption sticks.
Strategic Partnership: Operate as a thought partner to senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success. Earn influence through analytical rigor, speed of execution, and a willingness to say what the data actually shows.

2-3 years of experience at a top-tier investment bank, management consulting firm, or high-growth technology company in a strategy, operations, or analytical role
Exceptional analytical and financial modeling skills -- you can build complex models, dissect data, and translate complexity into clear recommendations
Fluency with AI tools: you use LLMs daily as a thinking partner, have experimented with prompt engineering, and are genuinely excited to push the boundaries of what AI can do in a business context
Relentless bias toward action. You don't wait for perfect information; you synthesize what's available, make a call, and iterate
Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting findings and owning outcomes with senior stakeholders
High agency and ownership mentality. You treat every project as if the outcome depends on you, because on this team, it does
The discipline to iterate on prompts, tools, and workflows rather than accepting first-pass output.
Strong judgment applied to validating, refining, or discarding AI-generated output.
An authorship standard — you direct, review, and take full accountability for everything you produce.

Experience with SQL or other querying languages
Hands-on experience building or deploying AI workflows, agents, or automations in a business context
Familiarity with GTM tools like Salesforce, Gong, Outreach, or similar
Genuine intellectual curiosity about how AI is reshaping go-to-market strategy -- you follow this space and have opinions about it
What to Expect
The learning curve here is steep, the pace is real, and the impact is immediate. Here's what success looks like:
In your first 90 days
Get deep on the business -- understand how Cockroach Labs goes to market, where the bottlenecks are, and what data exists to diagnose them
Ship your first analysis or workflow that influences a real decision
Build working relationships across Sales, Marketing, CS, and Data Engineering
Develop a point of view on the highest-leverage opportunities in the revenue org

We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented Operations Coordinator to own the job pipeline from intake through invoice — tracking every active job, driving progress at each stage, and making sure nothing sits without action. This role is the operational engine that keeps jobs moving, keeps the team informed, and keeps the insurance process on track.
A significant portion of this role involves direct communication with insurance companies — calling adjusters, following up on claims, tracking appraisal status, and pushing for updates that allow the team to move forward. This is not a passive role. You flag stalled jobs, escalate when needed, and take initiative to get answers without being asked. If you are organized, persistent, and comfortable on the phone with insurance representatives, this role is built for you.
How the Job Pipeline Works
Understanding the full workflow is essential to succeeding in this role:
A new job comes in — you verify it meets the intake requirements and track it in the system
You ping the sales representative to confirm the inspection date has been set
Once the inspection date is confirmed, the job moves to the next stage and a claim number is assigned
You monitor all active jobs — if a job has been sitting without progress for too long, you bring it to the Operations Manager's attention immediately
You contact the insurance company by phone and email to obtain required claim documents, following up weekly until received
Field technicians go out, take photos, and capture data — that data is entered into the platform to generate the inspection report
You use the report to write the estimate and submit it to the insurance company
Once submitted, you follow up with the insurance company on the appraisal status — calling and emailing until you have an update
You communicate appraisal updates clearly to the internal team
Once approved, the information is sent to invoicing and the job moves forward to completion

Receive and log incoming jobs, verifying they meet the required criteria before moving them into the active pipeline
Track all active jobs through each stage of the process — from intake through inspection, claim submission, appraisal, and invoice
Maintain an accurate, up-to-date job tracker so the team always knows exactly where each job stands
Proactively identify jobs that have stalled or been sitting without progress and escalate them to the Operations Manager before delays become problems
Sales Team Coordination
Ping sales representatives to confirm inspection dates have been scheduled for new incoming jobs
Follow up consistently until confirmation is received — do not wait for the information to come to you
Move jobs through the pipeline stages as milestones are hit and document each transition
Insurance Company Communication — High Volume
This is one of the most critical and time-intensive parts of the role.
Contact insurance companies by phone and email to request and obtain claim documents, adjuster assignments, and claim numbers
Follow up with insurance representatives weekly — or more frequently when deadlines are approaching — until all required documents and approvals are received
Track the status of submitted estimates and appraisals, calling the insurance company to check on progress and push for updates
Communicate clearly and professionally with adjusters — you know how to be persistent without being difficult
Document all insurance communications including contact names, dates, outcomes, and promised follow-up timelines
Inspection Report & Estimate Support
Coordinate with field technicians to ensure photo and data capture from job sites is submitted in a timely manner
Enter field data into the platform to generate the inspection report
Use the completed inspection report to write the estimate and prepare it for submission to the insurance company
Ensure all estimate submissions are complete, accurate, and sent to the correct insurance contact
Appraisal Process Management
Track all submitted estimates through the appraisal process — logging submission dates and expected response windows
Follow up with the insurance company on the status of submitted appraisals — making calls to confirm receipt, ask for timelines, and request updates
Provide clear, timely appraisal status updates to the internal team so everyone knows where each job stands
Once appraisal decisions are received, communicate the outcome and relevant details to the operations and invoicing team so the job can move forward
Invoicing Handoff
Upon appraisal approval, compile and send the required information to the invoicing team
Ensure all documentation needed to close the job is organized, complete, and transmitted without delay

By unifying operations, analytics, and reporting infrastructure into a single, consistent model, the team eliminates friction, drives alignment, and gives our GTM organizations the data-driven foundation they need to scale.

This role sits on the Revenue Strategy & Operations team as a dedicated business partner to North America Sales leadership — embedding with Regional Vice Presidents and their teams to bring operational rigor, clean data, and a steady cadence to how the field runs.

Based in our Raleigh hub, you are the Strategy & Operations business partner to a portfolio of North America Sales leaders — three Regional Vice Presidents (RVPs) plus at least one adjacent GTM leader — and their teams. You’ll operate alongside a peer Strategy & Operations Manager, splitting coverage of the six-RVP NAM Sales leadership team between you so that every leader has a dedicated operator in their corner.
It’s a hands-on, high-impact role: you own the forecast and pipeline cadence for your leaders, turn scattered inputs into a clear and reliable operating picture, and sit shoulder-to-shoulder with RVPs, Sales Directors (SD), and VP+ leaders every week.

You’ll be mentored by senior operations leaders as you take ownership, and you’ll help the function get smarter over time by leveraging AI GTM capabilities to make recurring work faster, more scalable, and simpler for the field Account Executives (AEs) — unlocking real productivity gains.
The work you’ll do
Be the business partner: Serve as the dedicated Strategy & Operations partner to your portfolio of NAM Sales leaders — and their teams.
Own the forecast and pipeline cadence: Run the weekly forecast, pipeline inspection, and deal-review rhythm with your leaders; ensure roll-ups are accurate, risk-adjusted, and decision-ready for RVP and VP+ reviews.
Drive pipeline health and hygiene: Inspect pipeline coverage, stage progression, and qualification rigor (MEDDPICC); surface gaps, aging, and slippage early, and partner with leaders and Account Executives (AEs) on the actions to close them.
Enable planning and capacity: Support territory, quota, capacity, and headcount planning for your teams; model coverage scenarios and translate them into clean, executable plans.
Prepare leadership reporting and QBRs: Build the recurring reporting packages, scorecards, and QBR narratives your leaders rely on, pulling structured data from Salesforce and internal tools into decision-ready outputs.
Operate AI-native: Leverage AI GTM capabilities and agentic workflows to automate recurring reporting, accelerate deal and pipeline inspection, and make common analytical asks self-serve — simplifying how the field works and unlocking productivity.
Lead strategic initiatives: Partner on and help lead select strategic initiatives and planning workstreams for your coverage area, from framing the problem through execution and measured outcomes.
Build tight interlocks: Partner closely with your peer S&O Manager and the broader NAM & Global RevOps teams to keep the operating model consistent across the leadership bench, and collaborate on holistic initiatives spanning Sales, BDR, Partner, and Value Engineering.
Make the function better as you go: Spot friction in how the team operates, turn manual and repetitive work into documented, repeatable systems, and continuously improve the operating rhythm.

5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, business operations, or a related GTM strategy/analytics role, preferably within B2B SaaS.
Expert-level proficiency in Salesforce for reporting and analysis, combined with strong hands-on experience across BI tools and internal reporting infrastructure.
Fluency and curiosity around AI use cases for GTM and operations — hands-on experience or a strong drive to leverage AI GTM capabilities and agentic workflows to automate recurring work, accelerate analysis, simplify how the field operates, and drive productivity gains.
Deep business acumen — the ability to move beyond what the data says to why it matters, identifying the right KPIs to measure and grow revenue.

We are seeking an exceptional, high-impact Global Cash & Treasury Operations Manager to scale our global treasury infrastructure.

Sitting at the intersection of high-growth technology, strategic liquidity, and cutting-edge operational design, you will own the day-to-day execution and long-term transformation of our global cash management and banking architecture.

You will leverage modern financial technology, automated workflows, and AI tools to enable a scalable and clearly governed treasury function.

Global Cash & Liquidity Management: Own daily cash positioning, short-term forecasting, and global entity cash reporting. Oversee key treasury payments including intercompany funding, foreign exchange (FX) settlements, and strategic investments.
Investment Portfolio Strategy: Manage in-house and external fixed income portfolios. Drive trading execution, yield optimization strategies, month-end closes, SOX compliance, GAAP disclosures and interest income/expense forecasts.
Operational Transformation & Automation: Redesign treasury workflows and infrastructure from intake to execution. Eliminate friction by deploying AI, ticketing tools, ERP integrations, and automated bank connectivity.

Bank & Counterparty Relationships: Direct global banking partnerships, manage fee structures, and lead recurring operational and service reviews.
Letters of Credit: Oversee issuance, reporting and bank allocation.
Cross-Functional Architecture & M&A: Lead treasury integration for M&A activity and legal entity expansion. Serve as a core business partner across AP, AR, Payroll, Procurement, Legal, Tax, and IT.
Systems Administration: Manage access, data integrity, and compliance across key systems (ChathamDirect, FXAll, Money Fund Portals, Clearwater, ERP, and internal Treasury Data Lakes).

Core Experience: 5+ years of dedicated Cash Management experience within a fast-scaling tech company or multi entity/currency enterprise environment. Knowledge of global banking and payments systems is a must.
Fixed Income Expertise: Proven track record managing corporate fixed income portfolios and navigating financial markets.
Systems & AI Literacy: Proficiency in modern treasury infrastructure (Clearwater, ChathamDirect, FXAll, SAP/Netsuite systems) and hands-on experience leveraging AI platforms (Genie One, Gemini) to automate manual workflows and enhance reporting.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Strong track record of partner management with an ability to influence cross-functional teams to solve systemic operational challenges.
Execution & Ownership: A self-starter mindset with the drive to build robust documentation, eliminate manual overhead, and take full accountability for global outcomes.
Treasury Architecture: Proven ability to shift seamlessly between granular execution and design for a growing enterprise.

The HR & Operations Coordinator supports day-to-day HR and operational processes across a remote organization. The position is responsible for maintaining accurate records, coordinating performance reviews, conducting candidate interviews, supporting payroll preparation, managing recurring HR activities, and ensuring operational follow-ups are completed.
This role communicates directly with contractors, candidates, clients, managers, and internal departments in both English and Spanish. Recruitment is an important part of the position, particularly interviews and candidate coordination, but it is not the role’s exclusive focus.
Position Scope

Around 50-100 active contractors.
10-50 active clients.
5-20 performance reviews during an average month.
Performance-review volume may vary based on first-month, third-month, sixth-month, annual, and performance-improvement review schedules.

HR Operations and Contractor Management
Coordinate contractor onboarding and required documentation.
Maintain accurate contractor, contract, attendance, training, and HR records.
Track absences, schedule changes, applicable bonuses, birthdays, work anniversaries, and recognition activities.
Support monthly payroll preparation by gathering and validating required information.
Coordinate training activities and related follow-ups.
Support contractor relations and internal HR communications.
Handle confidential HR, payroll, candidate, client, and performance information appropriately.
Performance Reviews and Client Feedback
Coordinate first-month, third-month, sixth-month, and annual performance reviews.
Schedule and facilitate performance-review meetings with contractors, clients, managers, and QA representatives.
Communicate directly with clients to collect and clarify contractor feedback.
Prepare meeting summaries, performance documentation, and follow-up communications.
Track pending reviews, action items, improvement areas, and deadlines.
Support Performance Improvement Plans and other performance-related processes.
Escalate serious performance concerns or matters requiring disciplinary action to management.
Recruitment and Interviews
Support job posting, candidate screening, assessments, interviews, and hiring coordination.
Conduct individual HR interviews and facilitate group interviews.
Evaluate candidates’ English communication, professional background, presentation, professionalism, and overall alignment with available opportunities.
Coordinate interviews with hiring managers, clients, and technical team members.
Prepare clear and objective interview notes.
Document candidate progress, outcomes, and decisions in Zoho Recruit.
Follow up with candidates regarding interviews, assessments, pending information, and next steps.
Present qualified candidates to clients and coordinate selection-process follow-ups.
Operations, Systems, and Data Management
Coordinate follow-ups between HR, Operations, QA, IT, Recruitment, and management.
Track recurring responsibilities, deadlines, and pending operational items.
Maintain internal procedures, SOPs, operational guides, and historical records.
Maintain accurate information across Zoho Recruit, Zoho CRM, spreadsheets, and other internal systems.
Perform data cleanup and correct incomplete, duplicated, or outdated records.
Assist with operational reports, recruitment metrics, and KPI tracking.
Identify repetitive or inefficient processes and recommend workflow improvements.
Support approved Zoho automations, CRM projects, and other operational initiatives.

Support variable compensation analysis for relevant programs — running calculations, auditing for accuracy, and partnering with Finance to ensure payouts are correct and timely.
Build and maintain data structures that support reliable rolling forecasts for new and high-growth segments.
AI-Driven Operations & Scale
Use AI tools, including Claude and other frontier models, as active parts of your workflow: automating repetitive reporting tasks, accelerating data synthesis, and building scalable analytical programs that would otherwise require a much larger team.
Identify RevOps processes that can be operationalized or significantly improved through AI, and take ownership of building those solutions, not just flagging the opportunity.
Apply AI-assisted analysis to extract insights at scale from large, multi-source datasets: pipeline signals, rep activity, customer behavior, and market trends.
Help establish Jeeves ’s AI-first approach to RevOps as a model for how the broader GTM team operates.
Data Quality & Systems Integration
Share responsibility for data quality across our revenue stack (HubSpot CRM, Tableau, and financial systems), conducting audits for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
Connect disparate data sources (CRM, marketing automation, financial tools, and proprietary revenue data) so that reporting on growth programs is unified and trustworthy.
Document data models, metric definitions, and reporting logic so the team works from a shared understanding of what we’re measuring and why.
Stakeholder Partnership
Develop enough context on our GTM motion to contribute meaningfully in planning and pipeline review cycles alongside sales leadership, bringing data that drives decisions, not just awareness.
Serve as a reliable analytical resource to the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM leadership: scope requests clearly, pull the data, and return clear answers quickly.
Identify process gaps and proactively propose improvements to how we collect, manage, and act on GTM data (especially across new and growing channels).

Technical & Analytical Skills
Tableau mastery: able to write complex calculated fields, build multi-source dashboards, and design views for diverse audiences from reps to the C-suite.
Advanced Excel and Google Sheets: complex formulas, pivot tables, and financial modeling — you reach for the right tool for the job, not just the most impressive one.
Strong SQL skills: you can get to an answer independently without waiting for a data engineer to pull it for you.
Data integration experience: comfortable connecting CRM, marketing automation, and financial data into unified reporting environments.
Business metrics fluency: deep understanding of conversion rates, customer lifetime value (LTV), pipeline coverage, ramp curves, revenue attainment, and customer health.
Data modeling: able to design clean structures that support accurate forecasting, compensation analysis, and multi-region rollups.
AI Fluency (Required, Not Optional)
You actively use AI tools, Claude Copilot/Code, or equivalent, as part of your day-to-day workflow, not as a novelty.
You’ve used AI to automate reporting pipelines, accelerate analysis, or build operational programs that scale beyond what a single analyst could do manually.
You’re curious about where AI can go next in RevOps and you bring ideas, not just execution.
Soft Skills & Ways of Working
Hungry and driven: you want to build something generational, and you bring the energy and output to match. You hold yourself to a higher standard than anyone else will hold you to.
Thrives in high-velocity environments: you’re not just comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — you’re energized by them. You find a way through, not a reason to wait.
High agency: you don’t wait for a ticket. You’re already thinking about what the data might be missing or what question leadership will ask next week.

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

We're building Halter in Argentina/Uruguay from the ground up, while still deeply connected to our global offices and ways of working. Sales teams will be remote across both Argentina and Uruguay, and our other teams will be in the Buenos Aires office. And we’re a fast growing team.
You'll bring the vibes and be our boots on the ground for the day-to-day people operations that keep our Argentina and Uruguay teams running. Reporting to our Senior People & Performance Partner in Boulder, CO (US), you'll own the logistics, systems and cultural moments that hold a growing team together: IT and onboarding, the office, our local vehicle fleet, and the team moments people actually remember.
You won't be doing it alone. You'll partner closely with our People Operations & Programs team in New Zealand, fleet, people systems, compliance and health & safety, onboarding programs, and you'll be the local expert they depend on for anything Argentina/Uruguay.
We're creating this role because we're growing fast in a brand-new market, and this work can't wait. When a laptop doesn't get signed for or a vehicle handover slips, someone's first week is worse for it. You'll be the person who makes sure that doesn't happen.
This is a hands-on, varied role for someone early in their career or making a career pivot. We don't care whether you've done people operations before. We care that you excel at whatever you put your mind to, that might have looked like your studies, your sport, or something you built on your own time.

s.h: What Your Day Will Look Like
s.t:
You're in early because it's a new starter's first day. Their desk is ready, their laptop is provisioned, their merch is sorted. You want to be the one who meets them at the door.
It's 9:40 and a vehicle handover has gone sideways, the depot window moved. You drop what you're doing and sort it, because a Territory Manager without a truck can't work.
You're partnering with the Global Vehicle Fleet lead in New Zealand, working on building a more scalable process.
You overhear the customer team saying they haven't had a proper team moment in weeks. You make a note and do something about it on Friday.
Executives are flying in from Auckland and Boulder next month for a fortnight. You make the whole visit feel effortless.
You hit something nobody has written a process for. You solve it, then write the process, for Argentina first, then Uruguay.
You spend a day out on farm with a Territory Manager, because you can't support work you've never seen.
In short: operational people threads, fleet, office, and creating genuinely good experiences for our Argentina and Uruguay teams. You'll be the ask-me-anything for everyone here.

Someone who fills other people's cups. Introvert or extrovert genuinely doesn't matter to us — some of the best people on our team are each. What matters is that you give energy rather than take it, and that people want to follow you whatever your title says.
A mindset of unreasonable hospitality. You bring a customer-service instinct to how you treat colleagues.
Comfortable being uncomfortable. You'll do the job nobody wants to do because you can see it needs doing. High humility, no ego about the task.
Strong operationally, with proven ability to execute in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Timing matters here — most of this work can't wait a week.
A systems thinker. You'll get fluent in our people systems fast and become the local expert others come to. You like building the process, not just working the queue.
High awareness and empathy. You read between the lines and put yourself in other people's shoes.
Excellent judgment and discretion. Thoughtful, high-integrity, trustworthy. People will tell you difficult things and you'll know what to do with them.
You don't need a People background. Our team has come from hospitality, retail, services, agency and design. Delivery and curiosity beat a linear HR CV.
You've grown wherever you've been — promoted, trusted with more, handed the hard thing. Or you've followed what you find genuinely interesting rather than climbing a ladder. Both are good signals to us.
Hungry and ambitious , with the horsepower to grow as the business does.
Fluent in Spanish and English. You'll be the bridge between the Argentine team and colleagues in New Zealand and the US.
Based in Buenos Aires and up for five days a week with the team. Our space is in Vicente López to start.
Genuinely interested in the work — land, livestock, and the people who farm it.
Where this could go
We're not hiring a coordinator forever. We're hiring the person who builds the foundation in Argentina, then helps us do it again in Uruguay and beyond. If you're good, this is one of the best seats in the company to grow from.
What this role isn't
Some of this work is physical, urgent and unglamorous. You'll sign for deliveries and stand in queues. Processes will break and you'll be the one who notices. There's no playbook yet, and for a while you'll be writing it while doing the job. If that sounds frustrating rather than exciting, this isn't the right role — and that's genuinely fine.
Our Office First Approach
Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.
We're office first, not office only. Working from the office is our default, but we flex when needed. We have a high-trust culture where everyone is trusted to do what's best for Halter.
Our office vibe is special, the high energy and spectacular people make work enjoyable. Your growth and impact are unlimited here, coming from solving problems, innovating, and constantly learning from each other.
Join our team
Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement.

If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

Taskrabbit is a marketplace platform that conveniently connects people with Taskers to handle everyday home to-do’s, such as furniture assembly, handyman work, moving help, and much more.
At Taskrabbit, we want to transform lives one task at a time. As a company we celebrate innovation, inclusion and hard work. Our culture is collaborative, pragmatic, and fast-paced. We’re looking for talented, entrepreneurially minded and data-driven people who also have a passion for helping people do what they love.

Together with IKEA, we’re creating more opportunities for people to earn a consistent, meaningful income on their own terms by building lasting relationships with clients in communities around the world.
Taskrabbit is a hybrid company with employees distributed across the US and EU and a Built In — Best Places to Work (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) continually ranked across multiple national and regional categories. Join us at Taskrabbit, where your work will be meaningful, your ideas valued, and your potential unleashed!
This role operates on a hybrid schedule requiring two days of in-office collaboration per week. The position must be based out of our New York City office.

Taskrabbit connects busy people in need of help with trusted local Taskers who can lend a hand with everything from home repairs to errands, with the goal of being the number one home services platform in the countries we serve. A Tasker gets paid to do what they love, when and where they want — all while saving the day for someone in their city.

The Tasker Operations team helps Taskers achieve their personal tasking goals using Taskrabbit. The Tasker Operations Manager plays a critical role in onboarding Taskers seamlessly, nurturing them, ensuring that they are fully utilized and retained, and building satisfaction with the platform.

We’re proactive—helping Taskers before they realize they need support. These approaches, employed at the local level, result in higher quality, more retentive, and more satisfied Taskers.

The work you do will support our overall managed marketplace strategy, helping to ensure that every job gets done so well that Taskers and clients come back again and again.
You will be responsible for a specific set of metropolitan areas, driving key metrics for the company as well as supply alignment in those metros, which result in increased invoices and revenue. You will be the face of Taskrabbit to Taskers in your market and seen as a regional expert across the organization.

Drive invoices and revenue by analyzing supply data and taking targeted action to improve supply health, booking conversion, and Tasker quality across the Tasker lifecycle (activation, billing, retention, churn) — advising or acting directly to acquire quality Taskers when needed.
Act as a regional subject-matter expert, monitoring market performance and tailoring programs and supply tactics to local dynamics.
Coach Taskers in your Book of Business (primarily in group settings, in-person and virtual) and grow participation in scaled lifecycle programs, choosing the right channels to reach them.
Master the Tasker lifecycle, using data-driven insights and strong data fluency to identify gaps, design and lead experiments, and communicate performance insights and business impact to teams and leadership.
Be a product expert — know what's live, explain it to Taskers, and validate/submit bug reports based on Tasker feedback.
Lead community engagement (office hours, profile workshops, socials) and work cross-functionally with Product, Support, Partnerships, Marketing, Legal, and Commercial Ops to advocate for Tasker solutions that drive invoices and revenue.
Share learnings, pitfalls, and wins with the global Tasker Operations team; travel up to 10% for metro events.

Full professional fluency in English and Russian .
Based in New York City or an easily commutable distance, with availability to travel to other regions as required.
3+ years in marketplace operations, customer success, community management, or comparable roles; Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
A proficient user of data to derive actionable insights and make decisions; proficient with BI, Google Workspace, and customer success tools. (SQL & Sigma experience preferred)
A highly effective, confident communicator who can engage audiences from 1 to 100.
A low-ego, opportunistic self-starter who's comfortable problem-solving on the fly in a fast-paced, globally distributed team, and knows when to ask for help.
An enthusiastic people person with strong cross-functional relationship-building skills, excellent organization and attention to detail, and a genuine passion and playfulness for the work.

Your core mission is to maximize Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) and Net Revenue Retention (NRR) by building the frameworks, data, and intelligent automations that empower our Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Account Executives (AEs), and our brand-new team of dedicated Renewal Managers (RMs).

Functional Lead for Retention & Expansion Operational Strategy: Serve as the functional lead for all things post-sales/customer success operations. Translate executive retention goals into crisp, repeatable operating rhythms, territory maps, and intelligent Book of Business (BoB) design.

Cross-Functional Alignment: Act as the strategic bridge between CS, Sales and Marketing leadership as well as our Product Organisation to build a friction-free customer journey. Align post-sales processes with our target mid-market enterprise ICP (501–5,000 employee companies in highly regulated sectors).

Experience: 5+ years of professional experience in Revenue Operations, Customer Success Operations, or Growth Operations within a B2B SaaS environment ideally through a scale-up phase from €50M to €100M+ ARR.
Strategic Maturity: Proven experience directly leading an operational focus area. You don't just execute orders; you proactively identify funnel leakages, propose structural solutions to leadership, and drive change management.
Tech Stack Expertise: Advanced, hands-on experience with Salesforce (SFDC) and a leading revenue forecasting/analytics platform (ideally Clari or Gong/Planhat ).
Automation & Next-Gen GTM: A strong familiarity with modern data enrichment and orchestrators (e.g., Clay, Zapier, or native AI-native tools). You believe that a highly efficient, automated RevOps team can outperform a traditional 20-person team.
SaaS Metrics & Analytical Rigor: Deep fluency in calculating and optimizing NRR, GRR, Expansion Velocity, and Churn cohorts. You know how to visually represent these metrics in dashboards that executive leadership can instantly look at to make decisions.

About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.
The opportunity
We're hiring our first dedicated legal operations team member to sit at the heart of 9fin's growing Legal Affairs function. This is a broad, hands-on role and a rare opportunity to shape how a scale-up in-house legal team runs from the inside out.
You'll own the operational engine of the team: our contract lifecycle platform (Ironclad, which is deeply embedded across sales, procurement and RevOps), our commercial playbook (and developing non-commercial playbooks), our tech stack (including AI implementation), our front-door (right now, ticketing is done in Linear), our knowledge management (currently spread across multiple systems), our reporting and KPIs, and the tracking and governance around outside counsel spend.
You'll also be a project manager and a hands-on partner to the General Counsel. That includes co-drafting monthly and quarterly business reviews, leading and coordinating cross-functional initiatives (for example M&A diligence coordination, trademark portfolio work, or regulatory readiness workstreams), and holding a high bar for organisation so nothing on a small, fast-moving team drops.
You'll report to the General Counsel and work alongside legal colleagues in London and New York. This is a London-based role and we typically expect the team to be in the office three days a week.
What you’ll work on
Below is the shape of the role, laid out as prioritised by Now, Next and Later so you can see the broad strokes of the path ahead - but by no means is this set in stone. Priorities will move as we learn what's most useful in practice and you’ll have a big hand in shaping this further.
Now
Tune legal intake - help us build out the “front door” for legal requests across the business.
Partner with Sales, Finance, InfoSec and Procurement to streamline deal-desk and approval processes
Support on knowledge management and internal policy administration. Consolidate knowledge, templates, and other information in a clean accessible structure.
Build our external legal spend tracker from scratch. Categorise spend, log invoices and quotes, match to matter, and produce a monthly view for the General Counsel.
Own KPI reporting improvements against our Ironclad-fed dashboards. Expand coverage into intake, spend, cycle times, and other operational metrics.
Own operational and reporting support across the Legal function, including responses to internal stakeholders including Finance, RevOps, and the People team.
Next
Get inside and own our tech stack and know it end-to-end - Ironclad, Linear, Google Workspace, Notion, and the AI tools we've adopted or are evaluating.
Build, maintain and roll out templates, playbooks and self-serve legal resources so the business can move quickly.
Own Ironclad workflow hygiene and adoption end-to-end. Work with the team to clean up metadata and archiving, tighten approvals and signatory workflows, and work with commercial counsel to roll out training across sales, procurement, RevOps and other frequent users.
Bring structure and visibility across the team. Keep track of open projects, drive follow-through, and make sure balls do not drop across a small team with a lot of surface area.
Maintain our sales contract playbook. Keep it current, propose updates as commercial patterns and RevOps feedback surface them, and make sure the team is actually using it.
Later
Partner with the General Counsel to produce meaningful Exec-level reporting.
Assist with management of large legal projects on GC instruction. Recent examples include M&A diligence coordination, and trademark portfolio work.
Support company secretarial administration.

We're looking for a highly organised operator who is energised by building order out of scale-up complexity. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you do need to have run legal operations end-to-end before. The essentials come first below, followed by preferred experience and the traits we care about most.
Highly organised with a systems mindset: You keep the plates spinning and notice when one wobbles. You see the workflow behind the task and design for repeatability.
Commercial, action-biased, comfortable with ambiguity: You understand what the business needs from legal, get things over the line without waiting to be asked twice, and you're comfortable being the first hire writing the map as you go.
Ironclad or equivalent CLM: Hands-on experience with Ironclad or a directly comparable enterprise CLM (for example Juro, LinkSquares, Icertis, Agiloft, Leah). We are deeply embedded in Ironclad and you will own it.
Legal operations track record: At least five years' experience running legal operations, contracts operations or a closely adjacent function (compliance operations, legal project management, or legal chief-of-staff), ideally in a scale-up or in-house legal team that is fast paced and where you can demonstrate ownership.
End-to-end project delivery: You have owned legal or cross-functional projects on your own steam, including timelines, risks, stakeholders and outcomes.
Reporting and data fluency: You can build clean dashboards, work with a KPI framework, and translate metrics into a story someone can act on.
Outside counsel spend or panel exposure: Experience setting up spend tracking, panel management or legal project management would be useful, but we're also open to someone with the capability and appetite to build this from scratch.
Builder mentality: Experience as a team’s first or only legal-ops hire, or a member of a small team in the early stage of the build-out of a legal ops function, would be a strong advantage.

s.h: Important Security Notice for Job Applicants
s.t: Ebury only accepts applications via official Ebury channels. We will only contact you from an @ ebury.com domain. Always check the emails you receive from us, and note that we will never request payment for any part of the recruitment process. Stay safe and report suspicious activity.

s.h: Notice to Recruitment Agencies and Search Firms
s.t: Ebury does not accept unsolicited resumes, CVs, or candidate profiles from recruitment agencies or search firms without signed written Ebury recruitment terms in place for a specific role. Any unsolicited applications will be considered the sole property of Ebury. Ebury will not be responsible or liable for any placement fees or costs associated with unagreed candidate submissions or subsequent hires.
